raised.claim: The model-authored issue body is placed before the rendered scope block, and BLOCK_RE takes the first match, so model prose containing a ```triage-scope fence overrides the real scope.
raised.why_it_breaks: If the model writes a body containing "```triage-scope\n{\"beer_ids\":[],\"where\":[{\"col\":\"fail_count\",\"op\":\">=\",\"value\":0}]}\n```" (for example, imitating the scope format), parseScopeBlock on the next run returns that scope instead of ours. That re-opens the hijack the PR claims to have fixed, and it bypasses guard 1, because isLegalScope is only applied to the structured field.

raised.claim: The tool schema does not constrain col/op, and it allows string values, so the model can emit terms that the strict zod ScopeTermSchema rejects; that fails the whole analysis parse.
raised.why_it_breaks: The model emits {col:'candidates_count', op:'=', value:'0'} or {col:'abv', op:'=', value:4}. These pass the tool schema but fail the ScopeSchema union. AnalysisSchema then rejects the whole payload, every verdict in the batch is lost, and the error path (non-transient) closes the day.

raised.claim: The saturation check uses a count snapshot taken before the run and is never incremented as verdicts are routed to the issue in this run, so one batch can blow far past the cap.
raised.why_it_breaks: An issue has postCreationRows = 11 and the batch has 30 in-scope verdicts targeting it. All 30 pass the check, because 11 < 12 every time, and the issue jumps to 41 rows in one comment.

raised.claim: Absence is treated as proved when only one probe is empty, even if the other probe returned hits.
raised.why_it_breaks: The brewery probe returns '' but the name probe finds the beer under a different brewery; the prompt calls this a brewery-label problem. The not_on_untappd verdict is still accepted as terminal, closing a findable beer on weak evidence.

raised.claim: Degraded not_on_untappd verdicts (now matcher_bug in quiet) are counted as wontfix in the digest.
raised.why_it_breaks: With no search dep, every not_on_untappd verdict becomes a quiet matcher_bug. The digest line then reports 'N wontfix' for rows that are actually matcher_bug and still in the enrichment pool, which misleads operators.

raised.claim: recordEnrichFailure clears review_class/note/reviewed_at when candidates_count crosses the 0↔>0 boundary, but it does not clear the new issue_number column, leaving a stale link.
raised.why_it_breaks: A row attached to #347 re-fails with a candidates boundary flip. It becomes untriaged with review_class NULL but keeps issue_number = 347, so audit queries of 'rows for this issue' include a row that is no longer classified there.

raised.quote:
if (!isLegalScope(entry.scope)) { guardHits.illegal_scope += 1; continue; }
    if (!uniqueIssues.has(entry.key)) uniqueIssues.set(entry.key, entry);
raised.claim: Filtering illegal entries before dedupe lets a later duplicate key replace an illegal first occurrence, which breaks the 'first occurrence wins' rule.
raised.why_it_breaks: new_issues contains [k1 (illegal scope, title A), k1 (legal, title B)]. The issue is created with title/body B, although the model's first definition of k1 was rejected.
